course.title: Forensic Reporting
course.description: A practical, standards-informed course on producing clear, traceable, reproducible, and defensible reports for digital and multimedia forensic examinations. It covers scope, evidence identity and continuity, integrity documentation, methods, findings, conclusions, limitations, exhibits, review, authorization, amendments, secure handling, and lightweight Python automation for structured reporting. It focuses on reporting and does not provide legal advice or replace validated forensic procedures.
prerequisites: Basic digital evidence concepts such as files, logs, timestamps, and hashes.
Ability to read JSON and tabular evidence records.
Awareness that real forensic work follows law, policy, and validated procedures.
learningOutcomes: Define bounded examination requests and scope.
Construct evidence inventories and chain-of-custody records.
Document methods, tools, configurations, integrity values, and deviations.
Distinguish observations, findings, interpretations, conclusions, and limitations.
Build traceable timelines with timezone assumptions.
Produce readable results, conclusions, exhibits, disposition, and authorization sections.
Perform technical and editorial release review and controlled amendments.
Use Python standard-library tooling to validate case records, hash files, and render HTML.
Complete an end-to-end synthetic forensic reporting project.

notes.text: Purpose and Role of a Forensic Report
SWGDE describes reporting as documentation of examination steps and results for review. Tool reports may support the examination report but normally do not document its entire scope.

items: A report should be concise, complete, traceable, and consistent with the underlying notes and evidence.
Do not turn an allegation into a forensic finding.

practicals.title: Hash a training artifact
practicals.description: Calculate SHA-256 before and after modifying a synthetic file.
practicals.steps: Create a file; calculate its digest; modify it; calculate again; record both values.
practicals.solution:
from pathlib import Path
import hashlib
p=Path("lab.txt"); p.write_text("training evidence",encoding="utf-8")
def sha256(path):
    h=hashlib.sha256()
    with path.open("rb") as f:
        for chunk in iter(lambda:f.read(1024*1024),b""): h.update(chunk)
    return h.hexdigest()
print("before",sha256(p))
p.write_text("training evidence changed",encoding="utf-8")
print("after",sha256(p))
practicals.output: The digest changes after the file is modified.

project.name: Controlled Digital Evidence Examination Reporting Pipeline
project.description: A standard-library Python utility that validates a synthetic, already-examined case record and renders a traceable HTML forensic examination report.
steps: Record evidence and findings with stable IDs.
Generate a SHA-256 digest for a local training artifact.
Review traceability, wording, limitations, and authorization.

code.report_generator.py:
#!/usr/bin/env python3 """Render a structured synthetic forensic case record as an HTML report.""" from __future__ import annotations import argparse, html, json from pathlib import Path from datetime import datetime, timezone REQUIRED={"case_id","report_title","request","evidence","methods","findings","limitations","conclusion","disposition","authorization"} def load_case(path): with path.open("r",encoding="utf-8") as f: case=json.load(f) missing=REQUIRED-set(case) if missing: raise ValueError(f"Missing required fields: {sorted(missing)}") return case def esc(v): return html.escape(str(v)) def rows(items,cols): return "\n".join(""+"".join(f"{esc(x.get(c,''))}" for c in cols)+"" for x in items) def render(c): ev=rows(c["evidence"],["evidence_id","description","source","hash_algorithm","hash","status"]) cu=rows(c.get("chain_of_custody",[]),["evidence_id","timestamp_utc","from","to","action"]) fi=rows(c["findings"],["finding_id","statement","basis","confidence"]) methods="".join(f"
  • {esc(x)}
    • " for x in c["methods"]) limitations="".join(f"
  • {esc(x)}
    • " for x in c["limitations"]) return f"""{esc(c["report_title"])}

    {esc(c["report_title"])}

    Case ID: {esc(c["case_id"])}
    Generated UTC: {esc(datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat())}

    Request

    {esc(c["request"].get("details",""))}

    Purpose: {esc(c["request"].get("purpose",""))}
    Scope: {esc(c["request"].get("scope",""))}

    Evidence Inventory

    {ev}
    IDDescriptionSourceHash algorithmHashStatus

    Chain of Custody

    {cu}
    IDTimestampFromToAction

    Methods

      {methods}

    Findings

    {fi}
    IDFindingBasisConfidence

    Limitations

      {limitations}

    Conclusion

    {esc(c["conclusion"])}

    Disposition

    {esc(c["disposition"])}

    Authorization

    {esc(c["authorization"].get("authorized_by",""))}

    Synthetic training report. This utility does not acquire evidence, replace validated forensic methods, or provide legal advice.

    """ def main(): ap=argparse.ArgumentParser(); ap.add_argument("case_json",type=Path); ap.add_argument("-o","--output",type=Path,default=Path("forensic_report.html")) a=ap.parse_args(); c=load_case(a.case_json); a.output.write_text(render(c),encoding="utf-8"); print(f"Wrote {a.output}") if __name__=="__main__": main()

project.explanation: The project separates case data from presentation. The JSON record holds reporting facts; the renderer validates fields, escapes inserted values, and produces evidence, custody, methods, findings, limitations, conclusion, disposition, and authorization sections. It deliberately does not acquire evidence or infer attribution. Real casework requires validated methods, laboratory controls, legal requirements, access control, retention rules, and local templates.
